question: Which method is also known as the ‘Income Disposable Method’?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Expenditure Method**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **expenditure method is also known as the income disposal method.**
 
• It's a** method of calculating a country's national income by measuring the final expenditure of all sectors of the economy.** 
 
• The expenditure method includes the following components: Private consumption expenditure, Government consumption expenditure, Gross capital formation, and Net exports. 
 
• **The expenditure method is the most common way to estimate a country's gross domestic product (GDP)**.
 
• The GDP calculated using this method is nominal GDP, which needs to be adjusted for inflation to get the real GDP. 
 
• To avoid double counting, the expenditure method only considers final expenditure. Intermediate expenditure on goods that are used for further production is excluded

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Product method**

 
 
• **Also known as the value added method,** this method calculates national income by adding up the monetary value of all final goods and services produced in an economy.
 
• **It takes into account the value added to a product at each stage of production. **
 
 
 
• **Income method**
 
 
• This **method calculates national income by focusing on the income received from factors of production, such as land and labour. **
 
• **While the statistical data and tools used to measure national income** may differ between these methods, they should all give the same result conceptually.
 
• If the methods do not give the same estimate, it may be due to a lack of relevant statistical data.
